title: Typing without looking
objectives: Place your fingers on the home row using the bumps on F and J
Name the finger that owns each letter key
Measure a typing speed in words per minute

screens.prose: Look down at your own keyboard. Run a fingertip slowly along the middle row of letters. Two of its keys have a small raised bump.

state.caption: The letter keys of a UK or US keyboard

screens.question: Tap the two keys with a bump.

hints.text: Feel your real keyboard. The bumps are on the middle row, not quite in the middle.
One bump is on the left half of this row, one on the right half.
The bumps are on F and J, the fourth key from each end of the row.

feedback.correct: F and J carry the bumps.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Feel the middle row on your own keyboard for the two raised keys.

byKey.middle: You tapped G and H, the two centre keys. The bumps sit one key further out, on F and J.
byKey.ends: You tapped the two end keys. The bumps are where your index fingers rest, on F and J.

explain.text: You found F and J. The bumps let your index fingers find their place without your eyes. Everything in touch typing starts from those two keys.

screens.prose: Rest your left index finger on F and your right index finger on J. Let the other fingers fall on the next keys outward, one key each. Thumbs rest on the space bar.
screens.question: Tap the eight keys under your fingertips.

hints.text: Four fingers per hand, all on the middle row.
The left hand covers these four.

feedback.correct: A S D F for the left hand, J K L ; for the right.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Four keys per hand on the middle row, with G and H left free.

byKey.whole-row: You tapped G and H too. No finger rests there; the index fingers reach across to them.
byKey.top-row: Your fingers rest on the middle row, the one with the bumps, not the top row.

explain.text: You placed eight fingers on A S D F and J K L ;. G and H stay free for the index fingers to reach. Your hands return to this row after every key.

screens.prose: The eight keys you found are the **home row**. Each finger owns its home key and the keys straight above and below it. Your left middle finger rests on D.
screens.question: Tap every key the left middle finger presses.

hints.text: Start at D and go straight up one row and straight down one row.
The finger's home key is D.
Above D is E; below D is C. So E, D and C.

feedback.correct: E, D and C: one column.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take D and the keys directly above and below it.

byKey.r1c4: R is above F, so it belongs to the index finger.
byKey.r1c2: W is above S, so it belongs to the ring finger.
byKey.r3c4: V is below F, so it belongs to the index finger.

explain.text: You took the column through D: E, D, C. Every finger works its own column like this. The middle finger never presses a key in another finger's column.

screens.prose: The index fingers are the strongest, so each covers two columns. One is its home column; the other is next to it, towards the middle.
screens.question: Tap every key the left index finger presses.

hints.text: The left index finger rests on F. Which column is next to it, towards the middle?
These two columns belong to it.
Column through F: R, F, V. Column through G: T, G, B.

feedback.correct: R, T, F, G, V and B.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Take the F column and the G column.

byKey.one-col: You took only the F column. The index finger also covers the G column next to it.
byKey.r1c6: Y is in the right index finger's area, across the middle.
byKey.r2c6: H is in the right index finger's area, across the middle.

explain.text: You took two columns: R F V and T G B. The right index finger mirrors this with U J M and Y H N. That is how eight fingers cover thirty keys; the thumbs keep the space bar.

screens.prose: You have just typed P with your right little finger. The next letter is not decided yet.
screens.question: Where should that finger go now?

options.text: Stay on P until the next letter
options.why: You left the finger up on P. From there every other key is in an unfamiliar place, so you look down.

options.text: Straight to wherever the next letter is
options.why: You skipped home. Fingers only know distances from the home row, so they must start from there.

options.text: Onto L, the nearest home key
options.why: L belongs to the ring finger. The little finger's home key is ;.

hints.text: Each finger's reach is learned from one starting key.
This is where the little finger lives.
After every key, the finger returns to its home key. For the right little finger that is ;.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Think about where every reach starts from.

explain.text: Every reach is learned as a move from the home row and back. If fingers drift, the learned moves no longer land, and your eyes take over. Returning home is what makes typing without looking possible.

screens.prose: On a real keyboard each lower row is shifted a little to the right. So B sits almost halfway between G and H.
screens.question: Which finger should press B?

options.why: You picked the hand that looks closer. B is in the T G B column, which belongs to the left index finger.
You let it vary. A key typed by different fingers never becomes automatic, so you keep looking for it.

hints.text: Which column is B in on this diagram?
B shares a column with T and G.
T, G and B belong to the left index finger.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Follow B's column up to the home row.

byKey.right: You reached across with the right hand because B looks central. It belongs to the left index finger, with T and G.

explain.text: B looks central, so many self-taught typists hit it with the right hand. On the chart it is in the T G B column, the left index finger's. One fixed finger per key is the whole rule; Y, on the right, is the mirror case.

screens.prose: Speed is measured in **words per minute**, WPM. Words vary in length, so a typing test counts every 5 characters as one word, spaces included. A one-minute test counts 200 characters.
screens.question: What is the speed in words per minute?

hints.text: How many 5-character words fit in 200 characters?
Fill in this cell first.
200 ÷ 5 = 40 words, typed in 1 minute.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Turn the characters into words first, then divide by the minutes.

byKey.chars: You gave the characters per minute. Divide by 5 to turn characters into words.
byKey.times: You multiplied by 5. Five characters make one word, so divide.

explain.text: You turned 200 characters into 40 words. Over one minute that is 40 WPM. Most people who type without looking reach 40 to 60 WPM.

screens.prose: You divided the characters by 5 to get words, then by the minutes. That is the whole formula: $$\text{WPM} = \frac{\text{characters} \div 5}{\text{minutes}}$$
screens.question: A three-minute test counts 450 characters. What is the speed?

options.why: You divided by the minutes but not by 5. That is characters per minute.
You turned characters into words but forgot the three minutes.

hints.text: Words first, then per minute.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide by 5, then by the number of minutes.

explain.text: 450 ÷ 5 = 90 words, and 90 ÷ 3 = 30 WPM. Both divisions are needed every time.

screens.prose: Ana's first backtest script is 60 lines, about 1,800 characters. Hunting for keys, she types 15 WPM. After a month of practice on the home row she types 45 WPM.
screens.question: How many minutes does touch typing save on this one script?

hints.text: Find the minutes for each typist: words ÷ WPM.
Fill in the last column first.
360 ÷ 15 = 24 minutes. 360 ÷ 45 = 8 minutes. Subtract.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out each typist's minutes, then take the difference.

byKey.slow: That is the slow typist's total time. Subtract the fast typist's 8 minutes.
byKey.fast: That is the fast typist's time. The question asks for the time saved.
byKey.wpm: You subtracted the speeds. Turn each speed into minutes first.

explain.text: 360 words take 24 minutes at 15 WPM and 8 minutes at 45 WPM, a saving of 16 minutes. That saving repeats on every script, every query and every note. Practise ten minutes a day on keybr.com and test yourself weekly.

ideas: Your fingers rest on the home row: A S D F and J K L ;. The bumps on F and J let you find it.
Each finger owns fixed keys, and returns home after every reach. B belongs to the left index finger.
Speed is words per minute, where a word is any 5 characters.
summary.trap: B looks central, but it belongs to the left index finger. Let each key have one finger only.

quiz.prose: You sit down at a new keyboard without looking at it.
quiz.question: Which two keys do your fingers feel for first?

options.why: You went for the centre keys. The bumps are one key further out, under the index fingers.
Those are the little fingers' home keys. The bumps are for the index fingers.

feedback.correct: The bumps on F and J.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Think about which keys carry the raised bumps.

explain.text: F and J have bumps, so the index fingers find them by touch. The other fingers line up beside them.

quiz.prose: A one-minute typing test counts 275 characters, spaces included.
quiz.question: What is the speed in words per minute?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide the characters by 5, then by the minutes.

byKey.chars: That is characters per minute. Divide by 5 to get words.
byKey.times: You multiplied by 5. Five characters make one word, so divide.

explain.text: 275 characters is 55 words of 5 characters. Typed in one minute, that is 55 WPM.

quiz.prose: The letter T sits in the top row, above G.
quiz.question: Which finger types T?

options.why: The left middle finger owns E, D and C. T is in the G column.
T is left of the middle line. The right index finger starts at the Y column.

feedback.correct: T is in the left index finger's second column.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find T's column and follow it down to the home row.

explain.text: T, G and B form the left index finger's second column. Its first column is R, F and V.

quiz.question: What is the speed in words per minute?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Divide by 5, then by 4.

byKey.nofive: You divided by the minutes only. That is characters per minute.
byKey.nomin: You found the words but not the rate. Divide by the 4 minutes too.
